title: Centrus touts unobligated uranium production in HALEU agreements
summary: In two recent announcements of partnerships with private microreactor developers, Centrus Energy Corp. declared that the high-assay low-enriched uranium it has agreed to provide both developers will be “unobligated,” meaning it will be produced entirely within the United States without use of foreign equipment or material. Centrus announced its multiyear contract with Radiant on September 9 and revealed a similar contract with Antares Nuclear on September 17. In both cases, Centrus noted that its AC100 centrifuge technology, which it will use to produce both low-enriched uranium and HALEU, originates in the United States and can be built using materials from domestic supply chains.

title: Supplier showcase: Framatome gives talk on modernizing safety I&C
summary: The American Nuclear Society recently hosted a Supplier Showcase webinar, “Modernizing Safety I&C: Practical Strategies and a Path Forward for Analog and Digital Systems,” featuring two speakers from Framatome: Logan Davenport, supervisor of product development and life cycle maintenance, and Erica Hindle, an I&C safety system software engineer.

title: Industry and INL collaborate to test new varieties of TRISO fuel
summary: In the 1950s, nuclear scientists set out to design a different kind of nuclear fuel. Instead of relying primarily on reactor systems and large containment domes to prevent the release of radioactive material, researchers in the United States and Europe envisioned surrounding tiny uranium particles with their own miniature containment systems. Over the next 30 years, they developed the earliest tristructural isotropic (TRISO) fuel designs, covering particles with multiple containment layers and demonstrating that they could operate at very high temperatures while maintaining strong safety performance.
